title: Snow
author: Wikipedia contributors
attribution: Wikipedia contributors, “Snow”, English Wikipedia. Text available under CC BY-SA 4.0; see source history for contributors.
paragraphs: Snow is a form of solid atmospheric precipitation consisting of individual ice crystals that grow while suspended in the air—usually within clouds—and then fall, accumulating on the ground, where they undergo further changes. It consists of frozen crystalline water throughout its life cycle, starting when, under suitable conditions, the ice crystals form in the atmosphere, increase to millimeter size, precipitate and accumulate on surfaces, then metamorphose in place, and ultimately melt, slide, or sublimate away.

Snowstorms organize and develop by feeding on sources of atmospheric moisture and cold air. Snowflakes nucleate around particles in the atmosphere by attracting supercooled water droplets, which freeze in hexagonal-shaped crystals. Snowflakes take on a variety of shapes, basic among these are platelets, needles, columns, and rime. As snow accumulates into a snowpack, it may blow into drifts. Over time, accumulated snow metamorphoses, by sintering, sublimation, and freeze-thaw. Where the climate is cold enough for year-to-year accumulation, a glacier may form. Otherwise, snow typically melts seasonally, causing runoff into streams and rivers and recharging groundwater.

Major snow-prone areas include the polar regions, the northernmost half of the Northern Hemisphere, and mountainous regions worldwide with sufficient moisture and cold temperatures. In the Southern Hemisphere, snow is confined primarily to mountainous areas, apart from Antarctica.

Snow affects such human activities as transportation: creating the need for keeping roadways, wings, and windows clear; agriculture: providing water to crops and safeguarding livestock; sports such as skiing, snowboarding, and snowmachine travel; and warfare. Snow affects ecosystems, as well, by providing an insulating layer during winter under which plants and animals are able to survive the cold.

sentence.text: Snow affects ecosystems, as well, by providing an insulating layer during winter under which plants and animals are able to survive the cold.
sentence.translation: 雪也会影响生态系统：它在冬季提供一层隔热层，使动植物能够在这层雪的下面抵御寒冷并存活。
sentence.analysis: 主句主干是 Snow affects ecosystems；as well 是补充语，表示“也”。by providing an insulating layer 是“by + 动名词”结构，说明影响生态系统的方式，即提供隔热层。during winter 表示时间。under which 引导定语从句，先行词是 an insulating layer，虽然两者之间隔着时间短语，which 仍指隔热层；介词 under 放在关系代词之前，表达“在这层东西下面”。从句主干是 plants and animals are able to survive the cold，be able to 表示“能够”，survive 在这里直接接 the cold，意为“经受住寒冷而存活”。

questions.prompt: 根据第二段，在什么条件下积雪可能逐渐形成冰川？
options: 雪只能积在没有山地的热带平原
所有积雪都在每年夏季完全融化
雪花不含冰晶而只含液态水
气候足够寒冷，使积雪能够年复一年地积累
questions.explanation: 第二段说 Where the climate is cold enough for year-to-year accumulation, a glacier may form。重点是跨年度的持续积累；may 也表示可能性，而不是任何一次降雪都会形成冰川。

questions.prompt: 根据最后一段，积雪层对某些动植物可能有什么帮助？
options: 使所有动物必须迁移到没有积雪的地方
形成隔热层，帮助其在冬季寒冷中存活
让植物和动物完全不再需要水
保证所有地区在冬季都没有低温
questions.explanation: 最后一句指出雪提供 insulating layer，动植物能够在这层覆盖下 survive the cold。文章描述的是雪层的隔热作用，并没有说雪会消除冬季低温。
